cards.prose: The last page of the prophets already said who would come before the great day of Yahuah (the LORD): *Elijah the prophet*. Right after it, Yahuah (the LORD) tells them to remember the law of Moses, so the one he sends comes to turn hearts back to the fathers and the Torah. John preaching in the wilderness is that sending.
cards.member_sentence: The closing word of the prophets promises Elijah before the great day of Yahuah (the LORD), and John arrives in the wilderness as that promise.

cards.prose: Elijah was a prophet sent by the word of Yahuah (the LORD) to meet the king while the land was starving, and from there he put the whole people to the choice between Yahuah (the LORD) and Baal. John comes the same way, out of the wilderness to a covenant people with one demand, that they turn.
cards.member_phrase: the word of Yahuah (LORD) came to Elijah in the third year
cards.member_sentence: Elijah is sent by the word of Yahuah (the LORD) to confront a king and call a people back, the pattern John follows.
cards.flag: The target verse itself only says the word came to Elijah to go and show himself to Ahab; the choice at Carmel that the old note names comes later in the chapter, so the card leans on the old note for that point.

cards.prose: John asks the Pharisees and Sadducees who warned them to flee, and then tells them to bring forth fruit. Yahuah (the LORD) said the same to the house of Yashar'el (Israel) in Ezekiel, judging *every one according to his ways*, and the way out is to turn from all the transgressions. Repentance here is a changed life, and nothing less.
cards.member_phrase: Repent, and turn yourselves from all your transgressions
cards.member_sentence: Yahuah (the LORD) calls the house of Yashar'el (Israel) to turn from all its transgressions, the same turning of a whole life John asks for.

cards.prose: Isaiah's chapter opens with *Comfort ye, comfort ye my people* (Isaiah 40:1), her iniquity pardoned, and then comes a voice in the wilderness clearing the road for the coming of Yahuah (the LORD) himself. Matthew puts John in the wilderness as that voice, at the front edge of the return Isaiah goes on to describe.
cards.member_phrase: Prepare ye the way of Yahuah (LORD), make straight in the desert a highway
cards.member_sentence: Isaiah's voice in the wilderness clears the road for Yahuah (the LORD) at the head of his comfort to his people, and John is that voice.

cards.prose: John called them a *generation of vipers* and asked who had warned them to flee. Yahusha (Jesus) says it again to the scribes and Pharisees in the temple, with the blood of the prophets spread out before them. It is the same word aimed at a system and the seed behind it, and John's own question still leaves the door open to any who turn.
cards.member_sentence: Yahusha (Jesus) later gives the scribes and Pharisees the same name John gave them at the Jordan, so the word was never a passing outburst.

cards.prose: John's *generation of vipers* and Yahusha's (Jesus's) *of your father the devil* name the same thing, a seed that does its father's work, a liar and a murderer from the beginning. He says it to men who *cannot hear my word* (John 8:43), so it is aimed at the system and its seed, never at the people as a whole.
cards.member_phrase: Ye are of your father the devil, and the lusts of your father ye will do.
cards.member_sentence: Yahusha (Jesus) names whose seed it is that does the father's work, which is what John saw coming to the water as vipers.

cards.prose: Behind the word vipers is the first enmity, spoken by Yahuah (the LORD) to the serpent in the garden, *thy seed and her seed*. When John turns on the men coming to the river, he is saying which side of that line their fruit shows them on, and his talk of trees and chaff in the same chapter is about the same sorting.
cards.member_phrase: between thee and the woman, and between thy seed and her seed
cards.member_sentence: Yahuah (the LORD) set enmity between the serpent's seed and the woman's seed, the line John's word vipers falls along.

cards.prose: The men who came down from Judaea made a mark in the flesh the door of salvation, saying that without it *ye cannot be saved*. That is the same shelter John tears away when he tells the Pharisees not to say they have Abraham for their father. John asks for fruit, and these men pointed to a credential.
cards.member_phrase: Except ye be circumcised after the manner of Moses, ye cannot be saved
cards.member_sentence: Men teaching that a rite makes a man saved are the same flesh credential John would not let the Pharisees hide behind.

cards.prose: Paul calls them *false brethren*, brought in quietly to spy and to put a man's standing under a mark of the flesh, and he gave them place *no, not for an hour* (Galatians 2:5). John saw the same sort coming to the water and refused them the same shelter. The bondage here is a flesh credential laid over the covenant, not the commandments.
cards.member_phrase: false brethren unawares brought in, who came in privily to spy out our liberty
cards.member_sentence: Paul names the men who slipped in to bind others with a flesh credential, the same system John met at the Jordan.

cards.prose: Paul warns against those who trust in the flesh, and in the verses after it he lists his own credentials, circumcised, of the stock of Yashar'el (Israel), *as touching the law, a Pharisee* (Philippians 3:5). These are the very things John says no one may stand behind. The warning is aimed at a teaching, and Paul himself is a Pharisee who turned.
cards.member_sentence: Paul warns against confidence in the flesh and then sets out his own credentials, which are what John says cannot shelter anyone.

cards.prose: Not every Pharisee who came stayed what John saw at the river. Here is one of the same sect, a ruler of the Yahudim (Jews), coming to Yahusha (Jesus) with his questions. John's word was aimed at the system that made them what they were, and a man standing in it can still turn and come.
cards.member_sentence: Nicodemus, a Pharisee and a ruler, comes to Yahusha (Jesus) himself, so a man standing inside that system can still turn and come.

cards.prose: The people first went over this river behind *the ark of the covenant*, out of the wilderness and into the land promised them. Matthew brings Yahusha (Jesus) to the same water just as John is calling the house of Yashar'el (Israel) to turn, so the Jordan is where the way home is walked again.
cards.member_phrase: the priests bearing the ark of the covenant before the people
cards.member_sentence: Yashar'el (Israel) first crossed the Jordan behind the ark, the crossing into the land that Yahusha (Jesus) meets again at the same water.

cards.prose: Yahuah (the LORD) told Joshua to *go over this Jordan* (Joshua 1:2), taking all the people into the land after Moses had died. Joshua bears the very name Yahusha (Jesus) does, and Matthew sets Yahusha (Jesus) at that river to begin his work.
cards.member_phrase: Yahuah (LORD) spake unto Joshua the son of Nun
cards.member_sentence: Joshua is commissioned to lead the people over the Jordan into the land, and Yahusha (Jesus), who has the same name, stands at the same river.
cards.flag: The shared name of Joshua and Yahusha (Jesus) is my own plain observation added to the old note's first-leader pattern; drop that clause if it should not stand.

cards.prose: Yahuah (the LORD) sent Elijah to the Jordan, and Elisha would not leave him, asking at that river for *a double portion of thy spirit* (2 Kings 2:9). Matthew sets John, the Elijah who was to come, at the same water, and the one who comes up out of it is the one the Spirit rests on.
cards.member_phrase: Yahuah (LORD) hath sent me to Jordan
cards.member_sentence: Elijah is sent to the Jordan and Elisha will not leave him there, the prophet's errand at the river that John's work at the Jordan repeats.

cards.prose: Naaman went down into the Jordan at the word of the prophet, *according to the saying of the man of Elohim (God)*, and came up clean. The river already carried cleansing at a prophet's word. John baptizes there with the people confessing their sins, and Yahusha (Jesus) comes down to the same water.
cards.member_phrase: dipped himself seven times in Jordan, according to the saying of the man of Elohim (God)
cards.member_sentence: Naaman is made clean in the Jordan at a prophet's word, showing the river as a place of cleansing before John baptized there.

cards.prose: John says the coming one brings both the Ruach HaKodesh (Holy Spirit) and fire, and Malachi says what that fire is. The one the people seek is to come to his temple without warning, and no one can be sure of standing in that day. He is a refiner of silver, working on the sons of Levi until what is offered is righteous, so the fire is a sifting and not mere ruin.
cards.member_phrase: he shall come, saith Yahuah Tseva'ot (LORD of hosts)
cards.member_sentence: Malachi's refiner's fire, the day of his coming and who can stand it, is the fire John says the coming one brings.

cards.prose: Yahusha (Jesus) says it becomes him and John to fulfil all righteousness, and Isaiah calls the one who comes *my righteous servant*, who bears the iniquities of many. The people confessed their sins at the water and he had none to confess, so he stands there already taking up the servant's work.
cards.member_phrase: by his knowledge shall my righteous servant justify many
cards.member_sentence: The servant of Yahuah (the LORD) is called righteous and bears the iniquities of many, the work Yahusha (Jesus) takes up when he is baptized.
cards.flag: Old note says the baptism is the public entry into the servant's righteousness; I kept that connection but did not use the word justify beyond the quoted phrase, to avoid the faith-alone grammar.

new_threads.title: The Jordan, where the people crossed and the prophets worked
new_threads.summary_md:
It ain't new. The river was already carrying this, and Matthew sets Yahusha (Jesus) where the older scripture had set the great turnings of the people.

*Then cometh Yahusha (Jesus) from Galilee to Jordan unto John, to be baptized of him.* (Matthew 3:13)

The people of Yashar'el (Israel) first came into their land through this water, with the ark going ahead of them.

*And it came to pass, when the people removed from their tents, to pass over Jordan, and the priests bearing the ark of the covenant before the people;* (Joshua 3:14)

The word that sent them over was spoken to a man whose name is the same name Yahusha (Jesus) carries.

*Now after the death of Moses the servant of Yahuah (LORD) it came to pass, that Yahuah (LORD) spake unto Joshua the son of Nun, Moses’ minister, saying,* (Joshua 1:1)

Then the prophets worked at the same river. Elijah was sent there, and Elisha went with him and would not turn back.

*And Elijah said unto him, Tarry, I pray thee, here; for Yahuah (LORD) hath sent me to Jordan. And he said, As Yahuah (LORD) liveth, and as thy soul liveth, I will not leave thee. And they two went on.* (2 Kings 2:6)

And a sick man was told to wash in it by the word of the prophet, and he came up clean.

*Then went he down, and dipped himself seven times in Jordan, according to the saying of the man of Elohim (God): and his flesh came again like unto the flesh of a little child, and he was clean.* (2 Kings 5:14)

So when John baptizes in the Jordan and the people come out confessing, the water is not a new place for a new thing. It is the river of the first entry, of the prophet's errand and of cleansing at a prophet's word, and Yahusha (Jesus) comes to it as the one leading the people home.
